questions.question: What is a key property of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It is used up completely during the reaction
It slows down the reaction to make it safer
It speeds up the reaction without being used up or chemically changed
It changes chemically to become part of the final product

questions.question: Why can we not use the same catalyst for every chemical reaction?
options: Catalysts are specific to particular reactions, meaning different reactions need different catalysts
Catalysts only work when dissolved in water
A catalyst can only be used once before it decomposes
Most reactions do not require catalysts because they happen instantly

questions.question: Which of the following best describes enzymes?
options: Biological catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells
Non-metal elements that conduct electricity in the body
Synthetic polymers used to make flexible containers
Tiny mineral pieces found inside metal ores

questions.question: What happens in a displacement reaction in solution?
options: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt
A less reactive metal displaces a more reactive metal from its salt
Both metals dissolve to produce oxygen gas
No reaction occurs unless a catalyst is added

questions.question: When magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution, what are the products of the displacement reaction?
options: Magnesium oxide and sulfur gas
Magnesium sulfate solution and copper
Copper oxide and magnesium metal
Copper sulfate and magnesium hydroxide

questions.question: How can displacement reactions be used to study metals?
options: To determine the melting point of different metals
To confirm the position of a metal in the reactivity series
To measure how much electrical current a metal can carry
To find out if a metal can be turned into a ceramic

questions.question: What is a metal ore?
options: A pure sample of metal found on the Earth's surface
A rock that contains a metal in a form that can be extracted
A mixture of different metals melted together
A synthetic material used as an alternative to metals

questions.question: Under what condition can carbon be used to extract a metal from its ore?
options: When carbon is more reactive than the metal being extracted
When carbon is less reactive than the metal being extracted
Only when the metal ore is a liquid at room temperature
Only when the metal is at the very top of the reactivity series

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical set of properties for metals?
options: Poor electrical conductors, brittle, and dull
Low melting points, soft, and transparent
Good thermal and electrical conductors, strong, shiny, malleable, and ductile
Highly soluble in water, soft, and gaseous at room temperature

questions.question: How are ceramics made and what are their typical properties after treatment?
options: They are made from hard metals that become soft when heated
They are made from soft substances that become hard and brittle when heated
They are made from liquid polymers that remain highly flexible when cooled
They are made from natural gases that solidify into soft structures

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: A pure non-metallic element with a high melting point
A mixture of elements that includes at least one metal
A type of ceramic made from heated clay and sand
A natural polymer extracted directly from plants

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of creating composites?
options: To ensure the material can easily dissolve in water
To combine materials to create a new material with improved properties
To turn metallic elements into non-metals
To speed up chemical reactions without using a catalyst

questions.question: How are polymers constructed?
options: By melting alloys together at extremely high temperatures
By joining small molecules called monomers together to form very long chains of atoms
By heating ceramic clays until they form crystalline structures
By extracting metals from ores using carbon reduction

questions.question: What effect does a plasticiser have when added to a polymer?
options: It makes the polymer much harder and more brittle
It gets between polymer molecules, allowing them to move over each other more easily
It creates rigid chemical bonds that lock the chains in place
It lowers the chemical reactivity of the polymer to prevent melting

questions.question: How do cross-links between polymer molecules affect the properties of a polymer?
options: They can make the polymer harder and less flexible
They cause the polymer to dissolve instantly in acids
They make the polymer extremely soft and liquid-like
They allow the polymer to conduct electricity as well as copper
